lines: My name is Mina.
I live in a small town near the sea.
Every morning, I walks to the beach with my dog.

why.en: With 'I', the present-simple verb has no -s.
why.ko: I 주어 현재시제 동사에는 -s가 없다.

gloss.en: My name is Mina. I live in a small town near the sea. Every morning, I walk to the beach with my dog.
gloss.ko: 내 이름은 미나야. 나는 바닷가 근처 작은 마을에 살아. 매일 아침 개와 함께 해변까지 걸어가.

lines: Tom has a little sister.
She is seven years old.
She like cats and draws them every day.

why.en: A she-subject in the present simple needs the -s ending, like 'draws'.
why.ko: she 주어 현재시제 → draws처럼 동사에 -s.

gloss.en: Tom has a little sister. She is seven years old. She likes cats and draws them every day.
gloss.ko: 톰에게는 여동생이 있어. 동생은 일곱 살이야. 동생은 고양이를 좋아해서 매일 고양이를 그려.

lines: There is a cafe on my street.
I go there on Saturdays with my friend.
The coffee are very good, and the cakes are cheap.

why.en: 'Coffee' is uncountable, so 'be' is singular.
why.ko: coffee는 셀 수 없는 명사 → be동사 단수.

gloss.en: There is a cafe on my street. I go there on Saturdays with my friend. The coffee is very good, and the cakes are cheap.
gloss.ko: 우리 동네 거리에 카페가 하나 있어. 토요일마다 친구와 거기 가. 커피가 아주 맛있고 케이크도 싸.

lines: We have a new teacher.
She is very kind and funny.
She has two dog and a big garden.

why.en: After 'two', the noun must be plural.
why.ko: two 뒤의 명사는 복수형.

gloss.en: We have a new teacher. She is very kind and funny. She has two dogs and a big garden.
gloss.ko: 새 선생님이 오셨어. 선생님은 아주 친절하고 재미있어. 선생님은 개 두 마리와 큰 정원이 있어.

lines: Do you like music?
I play the guitar in the evening.
My brother can sings very well.

why.en: After 'can', the verb is always in its base form.
why.ko: can 뒤의 동사는 늘 원형.

gloss.en: Do you like music? I play the guitar in the evening. My brother can sing very well.
gloss.ko: 음악 좋아해? 나는 저녁에 기타를 쳐. 우리 형은 노래를 아주 잘해.

lines: I get up early on weekdays.
My first class starts in nine o'clock.
I eat breakfast at home with my parents.

why.en: Clock times take the point-in-time preposition.
why.ko: 시각은 '시점' 전치사.

gloss.en: I get up early on weekdays. My first class starts at nine o'clock. I eat breakfast at home with my parents.
gloss.ko: 나는 평일엔 일찍 일어나. 첫 수업이 아홉 시에 시작해. 부모님과 집에서 아침을 먹어.

lines: Last weekend, I visited my grandmother.
We cooked soup together in her kitchen.
Then we watch an old movie on TV.

why.en: The story is about last weekend, so every action is in the past.
why.ko: 지난 주말 이야기 → 모든 동작이 과거형.

gloss.en: Last weekend, I visited my grandmother. We cooked soup together in her kitchen. Then we watched an old movie on TV.
gloss.ko: 지난 주말에 할머니 댁에 갔어. 할머니 부엌에서 같이 수프를 만들었어. 그다음 TV로 옛날 영화를 봤어.

lines: Look out the window!
It is snowing again.
The children is playing in the yard.

why.en: 'Children' is plural, so the helper before -ing is plural.
why.ko: children은 복수 → -ing 앞 be동사도 복수.

gloss.en: Look out the window! It is snowing again. The children are playing in the yard.
gloss.ko: 창밖 좀 봐! 또 눈이 와. 아이들이 마당에서 놀고 있어.

lines: My sister is two years older than me.
She is also taller than me.
But I am fastest than her at running.

why.en: 'Than' compares two people, so it needs the comparative, not the superlative.
why.ko: than으로 두 사람 비교 → 최상급이 아니라 비교급.

gloss.en: My sister is two years older than me. She is also taller than me. But I am faster than her at running.
gloss.ko: 언니는 나보다 두 살 많아. 키도 나보다 커. 하지만 달리기는 내가 언니보다 빨라.

lines: We are going to the beach tomorrow.
I will bring some sandwiches and fruit.
We don't have many time in the morning, so we need to leave early.

why.en: 'Time' here is uncountable.
why.ko: 여기서 time은 셀 수 없는 명사.

gloss.en: We are going to the beach tomorrow. I will bring some sandwiches and fruit. We don't have much time in the morning, so we need to leave early.
gloss.ko: 우리는 내일 해변에 갈 거야. 내가 샌드위치랑 과일을 가져갈게. 아침에 시간이 많지 않아서 일찍 나가야 해.

lines: Jun move to a new city last month.
He didn't know anyone there, so he felt cheerful at first.
One day, his neighbor invited him for dinner.
They talked for hours and soon became good friends.

why.en: 'Last month' is finished time, so the verb is past.
why.ko: last month는 끝난 때 → 동사 과거형.

why.en: Knowing nobody in a new city makes you feel alone.
why.ko: 새 도시에서 아는 사람이 없다 → 외롭다.

gloss.en: Jun moved to a new city last month. He didn't know anyone there, so he felt lonely at first. One day, his neighbor invited him for dinner. They talked for hours and soon became good friends.
gloss.ko: 준은 지난달 새 도시로 이사했어. 거기서 아는 사람이 없어서 처음엔 외로웠어. 어느 날 이웃이 저녁 식사에 초대했어. 둘은 몇 시간 이야기하다가 곧 좋은 친구가 됐어.

lines: Sara wanted to buy a gift for her mother.
She went to three shop, but she didn't find anything nice.
Finally, she chose a scarf because it was so ugly and soft.
Her mother loved it and wore it every day.

why.en: 'Three' needs a plural noun.
why.ko: three 뒤에는 복수 명사.

why.en: You choose a gift because it looks nice, and 'and soft' adds another good point.
why.ko: 선물은 보기 좋아서 고른다 — and soft도 좋은 점을 더한다.

gloss.en: Sara wanted to buy a gift for her mother. She went to three shops, but she didn't find anything nice. Finally, she chose a scarf because it was so pretty and soft. Her mother loved it and wore it every day.
gloss.ko: 사라는 엄마 선물을 사고 싶었어. 가게 세 곳을 갔지만 마음에 드는 게 없었어. 마침내 아주 예쁘고 부드러워서 스카프를 골랐어. 엄마는 그걸 아주 좋아해서 매일 둘렀어.

lines: I have live in this apartment for two years.
The rooms are small, but the view is wonderful.
Every evening, I sit by the window and watch the sun go down.
It is my favorite part of the day.

why.en: The present perfect is have + past participle.
why.ko: 현재완료 = have + 과거분사.

gloss.en: I have lived in this apartment for two years. The rooms are small, but the view is wonderful. Every evening, I sit by the window and watch the sun go down. It is my favorite part of the day.
gloss.ko: 나는 이 아파트에 2년째 살고 있어. 방은 작지만 전망이 멋져. 매일 저녁 창가에 앉아 해가 지는 걸 봐. 하루 중 내가 가장 좋아하는 시간이야.

lines: Mark has never been good at cooking.
Last night, he try to make pasta for his friends.
He forgot to add salt, so the sauce tasted delicious.
His friends politely asked for more salt.

why.en: 'Last night' is past, so the verb needs its past form.
why.ko: last night은 과거 → 동사 과거형.

why.en: No salt → the sauce had little flavor.
why.ko: 소금을 안 넣음 → 소스 맛이 없었다.

gloss.en: Mark has never been good at cooking. Last night, he tried to make pasta for his friends. He forgot to add salt, so the sauce tasted bland. His friends politely asked for more salt.
gloss.ko: 마크는 요리를 잘한 적이 없어. 어젯밤 친구들에게 파스타를 만들어 주려고 했어. 소금 넣는 걸 잊어서 소스가 싱거웠어. 친구들은 예의 바르게 소금을 더 달라고 했어.

lines: Yuna is going to visit her aunt this weekend.
Her aunt lives on a farm far from the city.
Yuna is excited because she loves animals and fresh air.
She will takes the early train on Saturday.

why.en: 'Will' is followed by the base verb, even with 'she'.
why.ko: will 뒤에는 she여도 동사 원형.

gloss.en: Yuna is going to visit her aunt this weekend. Her aunt lives on a farm far from the city. Yuna is excited because she loves animals and fresh air. She will take the early train on Saturday.
gloss.ko: 유나는 이번 주말에 이모 댁에 갈 거야. 이모는 도시에서 먼 농장에 살아. 유나는 동물과 맑은 공기를 좋아해서 신이 났어. 토요일에 이른 기차를 탈 거야.

lines: Our school has a small garden behind the library.
Students which want to help can join the garden club.
We water the plants every morning before class.
Last spring, we growed tomatoes and gave them to our neighbors.

why.en: Students are people, so the relative pronoun must be the one for people.
why.ko: 학생은 사람 → 사람용 관계대명사.

why.en: 'Grow' has an irregular past form.
why.ko: grow는 과거형이 불규칙.

gloss.en: Our school has a small garden behind the library. Students who want to help can join the garden club. We water the plants every morning before class. Last spring, we grew tomatoes and gave them to our neighbors.
gloss.ko: 우리 학교 도서관 뒤에는 작은 정원이 있어. 돕고 싶은 학생은 정원 동아리에 들 수 있어. 우리는 매일 아침 수업 전에 식물에 물을 줘. 지난봄에는 토마토를 길러서 이웃들에게 나눠 줬어.

lines: Leo was walking home when it started to rain.
He didn't have an umbrella, so he ran to the nearest bus stop.
While he were waiting for the bus, he met an old friend.
They were so happy to see each other that they missed the bus.

why.en: 'He' takes the singular past form of 'be'.
why.ko: he 주어 → be 과거 단수형.

gloss.en: Leo was walking home when it started to rain. He didn't have an umbrella, so he ran to the nearest bus stop. While he was waiting for the bus, he met an old friend. They were so happy to see each other that they missed the bus.
gloss.ko: 레오는 집에 걸어가다가 비를 만났어. 우산이 없어서 가장 가까운 버스 정류장으로 뛰어갔어. 버스를 기다리다가 옛 친구를 만났어. 둘은 서로 만나서 너무 반가운 나머지 버스를 놓쳤어.

lines: Hana's favorite season is winter.
She hates the snow, but she doesn't like the cold wind.
Every year, she make a snowman with her little brother.
They use a carrot for its nose.

why.en: 'But' sets up a contrast with not liking the wind, so the first feeling is a good one.
why.ko: but은 바람을 싫어하는 것과 대비 → 앞은 좋은 감정.

why.en: 'She' needs the -s ending in the present simple.
why.ko: she 주어 현재시제 → 동사에 -s.

gloss.en: Hana's favorite season is winter. She loves the snow, but she doesn't like the cold wind. Every year, she makes a snowman with her little brother. They use a carrot for its nose.
gloss.ko: 하나가 가장 좋아하는 계절은 겨울이야. 눈은 좋아하지만 찬 바람은 싫어해. 해마다 남동생과 눈사람을 만들어. 당근으로 코를 달아 줘.

lines: Daniel has work at the bakery since he finished school.
He gets up before sunrise to bake bread.
The smell is so bad that people wait outside before the shop opens.
He is often tired, but he enjoys his job very much.

why.en: With 'has … since', the verb is a past participle.
why.ko: has … since → 동사는 과거분사.

why.en: People only wait outside for a smell that attracts them.
why.ko: 사람들이 밖에서 기다리는 건 끌리는 냄새 때문.

gloss.en: Daniel has worked at the bakery since he finished school. He gets up before sunrise to bake bread. The smell is so good that people wait outside before the shop opens. He is often tired, but he enjoys his job very much.
gloss.ko: 다니엘은 학교를 마친 뒤로 빵집에서 일해 왔어. 해 뜨기 전에 일어나 빵을 구워. 냄새가 너무 좋아서 사람들이 가게 문 열기 전부터 밖에서 기다려. 자주 피곤하지만 일을 정말 좋아해.

lines: My grandfather teached me how to fish when I was a child.
We sat by the lake for hours without talking.
I found it boring at first, but later I understood why he loved it.
Now I go to the same lake whenever I want to relax.

why.en: 'Teach' has an irregular past form.
why.ko: teach는 과거형이 불규칙.

gloss.en: My grandfather taught me how to fish when I was a child. We sat by the lake for hours without talking. I found it boring at first, but later I understood why he loved it. Now I go to the same lake whenever I want to relax.
gloss.ko: 할아버지는 내가 어렸을 때 낚시하는 법을 가르쳐 주셨어. 우리는 말없이 몇 시간이고 호숫가에 앉아 있었어. 처음엔 지루했지만 나중엔 할아버지가 왜 그걸 좋아하셨는지 알게 됐어. 이제 나는 쉬고 싶을 때마다 그 호수에 가.

lines: Emma had a job interview on Monday morning.
She was such nervous that she couldn't sleep the night before.
She left home early because she didn't want to be late.
Unfortunately, the bus got stuck in heavy traffic.
She arrived early, and the interviewer was already waiting for her.

why.en: An adjective with no noun after it takes the other intensifier.
why.ko: 뒤에 명사 없는 형용사 → 다른 강조어.

why.en: The bus was stuck in traffic just before, so she couldn't be ahead of time.
why.ko: 바로 앞 문장에서 버스가 막힘 → 일찍 도착할 수 없었다.

gloss.en: Emma had a job interview on Monday morning. She was so nervous that she couldn't sleep the night before. She left home early because she didn't want to be late. Unfortunately, the bus got stuck in heavy traffic. She arrived late, and the interviewer was already waiting for her.
gloss.ko: 엠마는 월요일 아침에 면접이 있었어. 너무 긴장해서 전날 밤 잠을 못 잤어. 늦고 싶지 않아서 일찍 집을 나섰어. 그런데 버스가 심한 교통 체증에 갇혔어. 엠마는 늦게 도착했고 면접관은 이미 기다리고 있었어.

lines: Our town opened a new library last year.
It was build next to the old train station.
Inside, there is a quiet room where people can study.
My apartment is very peaceful, so I can't study at home.
That is why I go to the library every weekend.

why.en: The passive needs the past participle after 'was'.
why.ko: 수동태 was 뒤에는 과거분사.

why.en: Not being able to study at home, and going to the quiet room instead, points to a disturbing home.
why.ko: 집에서 공부가 안 되고 조용한 방을 찾아감 → 집이 방해되는 곳.

gloss.en: Our town opened a new library last year. It was built next to the old train station. Inside, there is a quiet room where people can study. My apartment is very noisy, so I can't study at home. That is why I go to the library every weekend.
gloss.ko: 우리 동네에 작년에 새 도서관이 문을 열었어. 옛 기차역 옆에 지어졌어. 안에는 공부할 수 있는 조용한 방이 있어. 우리 아파트는 아주 시끄러워서 집에서는 공부를 못 해. 그래서 주말마다 도서관에 가.

lines: Nina got home after a long day at work.
She was so tired that she could hardly keep her eyes open.
She decided to go to bed late instead of watching her favorite show.
She hoped to feeling better in the morning.
The next morning, she woke up full of energy.

why.en: She could hardly keep her eyes open, and she skipped her show — she went to sleep sooner.
why.ko: 눈을 뜨기도 힘들었고 프로그램도 안 봄 → 더 빨리 잤다.

why.en: 'Hope to' is followed by the base verb.
why.ko: hope to 뒤에는 동사 원형.

gloss.en: Nina got home after a long day at work. She was so tired that she could hardly keep her eyes open. She decided to go to bed early instead of watching her favorite show. She hoped to feel better in the morning. The next morning, she woke up full of energy.
gloss.ko: 니나는 긴 하루 일을 마치고 집에 왔어. 너무 피곤해서 눈을 뜨고 있기도 힘들었어. 좋아하는 프로그램을 보는 대신 일찍 자기로 했어. 아침에는 나아지길 바랐어. 다음 날 아침, 니나는 기운이 넘치게 일어났어.

lines: Last Saturday, Ben and his friends went camping by a lake.
They was setting up the tent when it started to rain.
The rain was heavy, so they stayed inside the tent.
They laughed, played cards and told stories until the storm stopped.
In the end, it was the most boring trip they had ever taken.

why.en: 'They' takes the plural past form of 'be'.
why.ko: they 주어 → be 과거 복수형.

why.en: Laughing, playing cards and telling stories is not how a dull trip goes.
why.ko: 웃고 카드놀이하고 이야기함 → 지루한 여행이 아니다.

gloss.en: Last Saturday, Ben and his friends went camping by a lake. They were setting up the tent when it started to rain. The rain was heavy, so they stayed inside the tent. They laughed, played cards and told stories until the storm stopped. In the end, it was the most exciting trip they had ever taken.
gloss.ko: 지난 토요일, 벤과 친구들은 호숫가로 캠핑을 갔어. 텐트를 치고 있는데 비가 오기 시작했어. 비가 세차서 텐트 안에 있었어. 폭풍이 멎을 때까지 웃고, 카드놀이를 하고, 이야기를 나눴어. 결국 그때까지 간 여행 중 가장 신나는 여행이었어.

lines: Mr Han runs a small bookshop that sell old books.
Business was slow, so he started a reading club on Friday evenings.
At first, only a few neighbors came.
Soon, more and more people joined, and the shop became crowded.
Now he needs fewer chairs because there aren't enough seats.

why.en: 'That' refers to one bookshop, so the verb is singular.
why.ko: that은 서점 하나 → 동사도 단수.

why.en: The shop became crowded and seats are short, so he needs to add some.
why.ko: 가게가 붐비고 자리가 모자람 → 더 늘려야 한다.

gloss.en: Mr Han runs a small bookshop that sells old books. Business was slow, so he started a reading club on Friday evenings. At first, only a few neighbors came. Soon, more and more people joined, and the shop became crowded. Now he needs more chairs because there aren't enough seats.
gloss.ko: 한 씨는 헌책을 파는 작은 서점을 운영해. 장사가 잘 안돼서 금요일 저녁마다 독서 모임을 시작했어. 처음엔 이웃 몇 명만 왔어. 곧 점점 더 많은 사람이 모여서 서점이 북적였어. 이제는 자리가 모자라서 의자가 더 필요해.

lines: If I had known about the sale, I would have go to the mall yesterday.
My sister went instead and bought a warm winter coat at a very low price.
She was pleased because it was so expensive.
When she showed it to me, I felt a little jealous.
Next time, I will check the sales before she does.

why.en: 'Would have' is followed by a past participle.
why.ko: would have 뒤에는 과거분사.

why.en: The line before says she paid a very low price.
why.ko: 바로 앞 줄 — 아주 낮은 값에 샀다.

gloss.en: If I had known about the sale, I would have gone to the mall yesterday. My sister went instead and bought a warm winter coat at a very low price. She was pleased because it was so cheap. When she showed it to me, I felt a little jealous. Next time, I will check the sales before she does.
gloss.ko: 세일하는 걸 알았더라면 어제 쇼핑몰에 갔을 텐데. 대신 언니가 가서 따뜻한 겨울 코트를 아주 싼 값에 샀어. 언니는 코트가 아주 싸서 기뻐했어. 언니가 코트를 보여 줬을 때 나는 조금 샘이 났어. 다음엔 언니보다 먼저 세일을 확인할 거야.

lines: Sam's computer stopped working the day before his big presentation.
He tried everything he could think of, but nothing helped.
In the end, he had to borrowed his roommate's laptop.
He was worried, but the presentation went very badly.
His boss said it was the best presentation of the week.

why.en: After 'had to', the verb stays in base form.
why.ko: had to 뒤 동사는 원형.

why.en: The next line calls it the best presentation of the week, and 'but' contrasts with his worry.
why.ko: 다음 줄 — 그 주 최고의 발표, but은 걱정과 대비.

gloss.en: Sam's computer stopped working the day before his big presentation. He tried everything he could think of, but nothing helped. In the end, he had to borrow his roommate's laptop. He was worried, but the presentation went very well. His boss said it was the best presentation of the week.
gloss.ko: 샘의 컴퓨터가 중요한 발표 전날 고장 났어. 생각나는 건 다 해 봤지만 소용없었어. 결국 룸메이트의 노트북을 빌려야 했어. 걱정했지만 발표는 아주 잘됐어. 상사는 그 주 최고의 발표였다고 했어.

lines: Ava used to hating running.
She would stop after a few minutes because she got out of breath.
Last year, a friend convinced her to join a running group.
Now she runs three times a week and feels weaker than ever.
She even enjoys running in the rain.

why.en: 'Used to' for a past habit is followed by the base verb.
why.ko: 과거 습관 used to 뒤에는 동사 원형.

why.en: Regular running, and even enjoying it in the rain, builds fitness.
why.ko: 꾸준히 달리고 빗속 달리기까지 즐김 → 몸이 좋아졌다.

gloss.en: Ava used to hate running. She would stop after a few minutes because she got out of breath. Last year, a friend convinced her to join a running group. Now she runs three times a week and feels stronger than ever. She even enjoys running in the rain.
gloss.ko: 에이바는 예전엔 달리기를 싫어했어. 숨이 차서 몇 분 만에 멈추곤 했어. 작년에 친구가 달리기 모임에 들어오라고 설득했어. 이제 일주일에 세 번 달리고 그 어느 때보다 몸이 튼튼하다고 느껴. 심지어 빗속에서 달리는 것도 즐겨.

lines: The village was quiet until a film crew arrived.
They were look for an old house to use in a movie.
They chose Mrs Kim's house because it had a beautiful garden.
For two weeks, the street was full of cameras and lights.
When they finally left, the village felt noisy again.

why.en: The past continuous is were + verb-ing.
why.ko: 과거진행 = were + 동사-ing.

why.en: When the busy crew left, the village went back to how it was before ('again').
why.ko: 북적이던 촬영팀이 떠남 → 원래대로(again) 돌아갔다.

gloss.en: The village was quiet until a film crew arrived. They were looking for an old house to use in a movie. They chose Mrs Kim's house because it had a beautiful garden. For two weeks, the street was full of cameras and lights. When they finally left, the village felt quiet again.
gloss.ko: 촬영팀이 오기 전까지 마을은 조용했어. 그들은 영화에 쓸 오래된 집을 찾고 있었어. 정원이 아름다워서 김 씨 아주머니 댁을 골랐어. 두 주 동안 거리는 카메라와 조명으로 가득했어. 마침내 그들이 떠나자 마을은 다시 조용해졌어.

lines: Our neighbor's dog barks every time someone walk past the house.
Last night, it barked for hours, and nobody could sleep.
This morning, my father went to talk to the neighbor politely.
The neighbor apologized and promised to keep the dog inside at night.
That night, everyone on the street finally slept badly.

why.en: 'Someone' is singular, so the present-simple verb takes -s.
why.ko: someone은 단수 → 현재시제 동사에 -s.

why.en: The dog was kept inside after the promise, and 'finally' marks a change for the better.
why.ko: 약속대로 개를 안에 둠, finally는 좋아진 변화.

gloss.en: Our neighbor's dog barks every time someone walks past the house. Last night, it barked for hours, and nobody could sleep. This morning, my father went to talk to the neighbor politely. The neighbor apologized and promised to keep the dog inside at night. That night, everyone on the street finally slept well.
gloss.ko: 이웃집 개는 누가 집 앞을 지나갈 때마다 짖어. 어젯밤엔 몇 시간이나 짖어서 아무도 못 잤어. 오늘 아침 아빠가 이웃에게 정중하게 말하러 갔어. 이웃은 사과하고 밤에는 개를 안에 두겠다고 약속했어. 그날 밤, 거리 사람들 모두 마침내 푹 잤어.

lines: When Clara first moved abroad, she couldn't speak a word of the local language.
Ordering food was a challenge, so she often pointed at pictures on the menu.
Once she had settled in, she signed up for evening classes.
She did many mistakes, but she never gave up.
Within a year, she could chat easily with the shop owners on her street.
Looking back, she wishes she had started learning after she arrived.

why.en: 'Mistakes' collocates with a different verb than 'do'.
why.ko: mistake와 짝이 되는 동사는 do가 아니다.

why.en: She already started after settling in, so the regret must be about starting earlier.
why.ko: 이미 자리 잡은 뒤에 시작함 → 아쉬움은 더 일찍 시작하지 않은 것.

gloss.en: When Clara first moved abroad, she couldn't speak a word of the local language. Ordering food was a challenge, so she often pointed at pictures on the menu. Once she had settled in, she signed up for evening classes. She made many mistakes, but she never gave up. Within a year, she could chat easily with the shop owners on her street. Looking back, she wishes she had started learning before she arrived.
gloss.ko: 클라라가 처음 외국으로 이사했을 때 그 나라 말을 한마디도 못 했어. 음식 주문도 힘들어서 메뉴 사진을 손가락으로 가리키곤 했어. 자리를 잡은 뒤 저녁 수업에 등록했어. 실수를 많이 했지만 포기하지 않았어. 1년도 안 돼 동네 가게 주인들과 편하게 수다를 떨 수 있게 됐어. 돌아보면, 오기 전에 배우기 시작했으면 좋았겠다고 생각해.

lines: Tom had always dream of opening his own café.
For years, he saved money and took cooking classes at night.
When he finally opened it, the first few weeks were very quiet.
He was close to giving up, but then a local blogger wrote a glowing review.
Suddenly, there was a line outside the door every morning.
If the review hadn't appeared, he might have expanded the business.

why.en: The past perfect is had + past participle.
why.ko: 과거완료 = had + 과거분사.

why.en: Without the review, the quiet weeks and his near giving up would have continued.
why.ko: 후기가 없었다면 손님 없던 몇 주와 포기 직전 상태가 이어졌을 것.

gloss.en: Tom had always dreamed of opening his own café. For years, he saved money and took cooking classes at night. When he finally opened it, the first few weeks were very quiet. He was close to giving up, but then a local blogger wrote a glowing review. Suddenly, there was a line outside the door every morning. If the review hadn't appeared, he might have closed the business.
gloss.ko: 톰은 늘 자기 카페를 여는 꿈을 꿔 왔어. 몇 년 동안 돈을 모으고 밤에는 요리 수업을 들었어. 마침내 카페를 열었을 때 처음 몇 주는 손님이 거의 없었어. 포기하기 직전이었는데, 그때 동네 블로거가 극찬하는 후기를 썼어. 갑자기 매일 아침 문 밖에 줄이 생겼어. 그 후기가 없었다면 그는 가게를 닫았을지도 몰라.

lines: Not having visit the city before, Lena relied on her phone for directions.
Unfortunately, the battery ran out just as she left the station.
She asked a stranger for help, and he kindly drew her a map.
The map was so detailed that she found her hotel without any trouble.
Thanks to him, she even arrived in time for dinner.
Admittedly, she had been nervous at first; even so, the day turned out to be a terrible surprise.

why.en: A perfect participle clause is 'having' + past participle.
why.ko: 완료 분사구문 = having + 과거분사.

why.en: A kind stranger, an easy walk to the hotel and dinner on time make the day a good one.
why.ko: 친절한 사람, 쉽게 찾은 호텔, 제때 저녁 → 좋은 하루.

gloss.en: Not having visited the city before, Lena relied on her phone for directions. Unfortunately, the battery ran out just as she left the station. She asked a stranger for help, and he kindly drew her a map. The map was so detailed that she found her hotel without any trouble. Thanks to him, she even arrived in time for dinner. Admittedly, she had been nervous at first; even so, the day turned out to be a pleasant surprise.
gloss.ko: 그 도시에 와 본 적이 없어서 레나는 길 찾기를 휴대폰에 의지했어. 그런데 역을 나서자마자 배터리가 다 됐어. 낯선 사람에게 도움을 청했더니 친절하게 지도를 그려 줬어. 지도가 아주 자세해서 레나는 쉽게 호텔을 찾았어. 그 사람 덕분에 저녁 시간에도 늦지 않았어. 처음엔 불안했던 게 사실이지만, 그래도 그날은 뜻밖의 즐거운 하루가 됐어.

lines: Ryan's team had been work on the project for months.
The night before the deadline, they discovered a serious problem in the design.
Instead of panicking, Ryan asked everyone to stay calm and focus.
They worked until sunrise and fixed it just in time.
The client was impressed by the final result.
Ryan still says that relaxing night taught the team more than any training course.

why.en: 'Had been' for an ongoing action is followed by the -ing form.
why.ko: 계속된 일 had been 뒤에는 -ing.

why.en: A serious problem before a deadline and working until sunrise make a hard night, not an easy one.
why.ko: 마감 전 심각한 문제, 해 뜰 때까지 일함 → 편한 밤이 아니다.

gloss.en: Ryan's team had been working on the project for months. The night before the deadline, they discovered a serious problem in the design. Instead of panicking, Ryan asked everyone to stay calm and focus. They worked until sunrise and fixed it just in time. The client was impressed by the final result. Ryan still says that stressful night taught the team more than any training course.
gloss.ko: 라이언의 팀은 몇 달째 그 프로젝트를 해 오고 있었어. 마감 전날 밤, 설계에서 심각한 문제를 발견했어. 라이언은 당황하는 대신 모두에게 침착하게 집중하자고 했어. 그들은 해 뜰 때까지 일해서 겨우 시간에 맞춰 고쳤어. 고객은 최종 결과에 감탄했어. 라이언은 지금도 그 힘들었던 밤이 어떤 연수보다 팀에게 많은 걸 가르쳐 줬다고 말해.

lines: What surprised me most about the trip was how rude everyone was.
On the first day, our car broke down on a narrow mountain road.
Within minutes, a farmer stopped and offered to tow us to the next village.
His wife insisted that we stay for lunch while the car was being repaired.
They refused to accept any money, no matter how hard we tried.
Had it not be for their kindness, the trip would have been a disaster.

why.en: Everyone in the story helps, feeds and refuses payment — the opposite of bad manners.
why.ko: 이야기 속 사람들은 돕고, 밥을 주고, 돈도 안 받음 → 무례함과 반대.

why.en: The inverted conditional 'Had it not …' needs a past participle.
why.ko: 도치 조건 Had it not … 뒤에는 과거분사.

gloss.en: What surprised me most about the trip was how friendly everyone was. On the first day, our car broke down on a narrow mountain road. Within minutes, a farmer stopped and offered to tow us to the next village. His wife insisted that we stay for lunch while the car was being repaired. They refused to accept any money, no matter how hard we tried. Had it not been for their kindness, the trip would have been a disaster.
gloss.ko: 여행에서 가장 놀라웠던 건 모두가 얼마나 친절했는지였어. 첫날, 좁은 산길에서 차가 고장 났어. 몇 분 만에 한 농부가 차를 세우고 다음 마을까지 끌어 주겠다고 했어. 차를 고치는 동안 농부의 아내는 꼭 점심을 먹고 가라고 했어. 아무리 애써도 그들은 돈을 한 푼도 받지 않았어. 그들의 친절이 없었다면 여행은 엉망이 됐을 거야.

lines: The decide to move the office to the suburbs was not popular at first.
Many staff members complained about the longer journey to work.
However, the new building had a large garden and plenty of natural light.
Over time, people began to appreciate the calmer surroundings.
Some even said that they felt more productive than before.
It seems that the move was, on the whole, a foolish choice.

why.en: After 'The' and before 'to', a noun is needed.
why.ko: The 뒤, to 앞에는 명사.

why.en: People came to like the new place and worked better, so the move turned out well.
why.ko: 사람들이 새 곳을 좋아하고 일도 더 잘됨 → 잘한 이전.

gloss.en: The decision to move the office to the suburbs was not popular at first. Many staff members complained about the longer journey to work. However, the new building had a large garden and plenty of natural light. Over time, people began to appreciate the calmer surroundings. Some even said that they felt more productive than before. It seems that the move was, on the whole, a wise choice.
gloss.ko: 사무실을 교외로 옮기기로 한 결정은 처음엔 인기가 없었어. 많은 직원들이 출근길이 길어졌다고 불평했어. 하지만 새 건물에는 넓은 정원과 햇빛이 충분했어. 시간이 지나면서 사람들은 더 차분한 주변 환경을 좋아하게 됐어. 전보다 일이 더 잘된다는 사람도 있었어. 전체적으로 보면 이전은 현명한 선택이었던 것 같아.

lines: Admittedly, I was skeptical when my friend suggested a silent retreat.
Spending a whole weekend without talking sounded impossible to me.
The first day was difficult, and I kept wanting to check my phone.
By the second day, though, my mind had became surprisingly calm.
I noticed sounds I usually ignore, like birds and the wind in the trees.
I came home feeling angrier than I had in months.

why.en: After 'had', use the past participle.
why.ko: had 뒤에는 과거분사.

why.en: The writer's mind had grown calm and quiet sounds became a pleasure, so the trip ended in peace, not irritation.
why.ko: 마음이 차분해지고 조용한 소리를 즐김 → 짜증이 아니라 평온하게 돌아왔다.

gloss.en: Admittedly, I was skeptical when my friend suggested a silent retreat. Spending a whole weekend without talking sounded impossible to me. The first day was difficult, and I kept wanting to check my phone. By the second day, though, my mind had become surprisingly calm. I noticed sounds I usually ignore, like birds and the wind in the trees. I came home feeling calmer than I had in months.
gloss.ko: 솔직히 친구가 말 없는 수련회를 제안했을 때 반신반의했어. 주말 내내 말을 안 한다는 게 불가능해 보였거든. 첫날은 힘들었고 계속 휴대폰을 보고 싶었어. 그런데 둘째 날이 되자 마음이 놀랄 만큼 차분해졌어. 평소엔 흘려듣던 새소리나 나무 사이 바람 소리가 들렸어. 몇 달 만에 가장 차분한 마음으로 집에 돌아왔어.

lines: It would appear that the town's old cinema will finally reopen.
It closed years ago, when fewer people went out to watch films.
A group of residents raised the money needing to restore the building.
Their efforts were praised in the local newspaper.
The first screening is planned for next month, and the tickets have already sold out.
Clearly, nobody in town is interested in the project.

why.en: The money is what the building requires, so the participle must be passive.
why.ko: 돈은 건물에 '필요한' 것 → 수동 분사.

why.en: Residents raised money and the tickets sold out, so the town clearly cares.
why.ko: 주민들이 돈을 모으고 표가 매진됨 → 마을 사람들이 관심이 많다.

gloss.en: It would appear that the town's old cinema will finally reopen. It closed years ago, when fewer people went out to watch films. A group of residents raised the money needed to restore the building. Their efforts were praised in the local newspaper. The first screening is planned for next month, and the tickets have already sold out. Clearly, everyone in town is interested in the project.
gloss.ko: 마을의 오래된 극장이 마침내 다시 문을 여는 것 같아. 극장은 사람들이 영화를 보러 덜 나가던 몇 년 전에 문을 닫았어. 주민 몇 명이 건물을 복원하는 데 필요한 돈을 모았어. 그들의 노력은 지역 신문에서 칭찬을 받았어. 첫 상영은 다음 달로 잡혀 있는데 표가 벌써 다 팔렸어. 마을 사람 모두가 이 일에 관심이 있는 게 분명해.

lines: Lucy had never cook for more than two people before.
So when her parents asked her to host the family dinner, she panicked.
She spent the whole week planning the menu and practicing recipes.
On the day, the oven broke and the rice burned.
Instead of giving up, she ordered pizza and laughed about it with everyone.
Her parents said it was the most boring dinner they had ever had.

why.en: 'Had never' is followed by a past participle.
why.ko: had never 뒤에는 과거분사.

why.en: A broken oven, burned rice and a pizza everyone laughed about make a night people remember.
why.ko: 고장 난 오븐, 탄 밥, 다 같이 웃은 피자 → 기억에 남는 밤.

gloss.en: Lucy had never cooked for more than two people before. So when her parents asked her to host the family dinner, she panicked. She spent the whole week planning the menu and practicing recipes. On the day, the oven broke and the rice burned. Instead of giving up, she ordered pizza and laughed about it with everyone. Her parents said it was the most memorable dinner they had ever had.
gloss.ko: 루시는 그때까지 두 명 넘게 요리해 준 적이 없었어. 그래서 부모님이 가족 저녁 식사를 맡아 달라고 했을 때 당황했어. 일주일 내내 메뉴를 짜고 요리를 연습했어. 당일, 오븐이 고장 나고 밥이 탔어. 루시는 포기하는 대신 피자를 시키고 모두와 함께 웃어넘겼어. 부모님은 그날이 지금까지 가장 기억에 남는 저녁이었다고 했어.
